messages:
oliver: FYI after the morning maintenance some tiny GPU pods are stuck Pending even though nodes report spare fractional GPU capacity. Looks like fragmentation + anti-affinity is blocking binpack.

maria: Can you paste the pod spec? nodeSelector/affinity/requests?

oliver: snippet: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: micro-infer-7
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    gpu-type: a100
  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: inference
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
  resources:
    requests:
      nvidia.com/gpu: "0.125"
```

kevin: fractional requests at 0.125. Our scheduler's strict host-level podAntiAffinity combined with leftover fragments from warm-pool drains will prevent co-location. Which nodes are showing the leftovers?

oliver: a few nodes in pool-gpu-eu-west1b: allocatable shows free fragments of 0.0625-0.25 after the rolling cordon/drain. Controller uncordoned a couple of nodes while some PVCs were still attached, so pods couldn't be rescheduled off host.

anita: Warm-pool flow: cordon -> drain -> maintenance -> uncordon. If PV detach lags, pods remain bound and leave tiny unusable GPU fragments. The warmpool controller uses --pod-deletion-timeout=300s by default which magnifies the window.

raj: Two possible levers: (A) reduce grace/deletion timeout for low-priority warmpool pods (B) make scheduler treat podAntiAffinity as soft for pods with GPU < 0.5 and priorityClass=low. The latter avoids noisy-neighbor issues for higher priority traffic.

kevin: We previously experimented with softening anti-affinity and saw better packing but occasional latency spikes under dense packing. Need a measured canary before changing defaults.

maria: short-term mitigation: can infra run a "pack coalesce" controller that finds low-priority fractional pods and temporarily patches their anti-affinity required -> preferred when a drain event is detected? That would be reversible and narrow.

oliver: I can prototype: controller looks for pods with labels {app:inference, priority:low} and nvidia.com/gpu < 0.5, adds annotation coalesce/override=true and rewrites affinity to preferred for up to 10m.

anita: Watch out for PVs. If PVs are involved we need to ensure not to move pods that require host-local storage. Filter those out.

infra-bot: scheduled: canary/pack-coalesce/1766666001 (30 pods) queued on nodes: node-12,node-15,node-18.

raj: Also propose a scheduler plugin tweak: scoring adjustment that reduces penalty for inter-pod anti-affinity when pod.Requests.GPU < 0.5. Keep it configurable and gated behind feature-flag.

kevin: Action plan: (1) oliver run non-prod force-delete/evict of micro-infer* and kick off pack-coalesce canary (2) infra run density telemetry collecting gpu_mem, gpu_util, host_cpu, and p99/p95 model latency on dense nodes (3) raj/scheduler to draft plugin prototype and run A/B canary.

maria: Please avoid force-delete on any customer-facing inference pods. Which namespaces have these tiny pods?

oliver: Only infra-test and batch-low namespaces in staging. No customer impact. I'll proceed in staging.

anita: For warmpool fix I like decreasing warmpool controller drain timeout to 30s for low-priority nodes, but pair it with PV-detach cleanup job to avoid orphan mounts.

oliver: I'll run the staging canary now and post telemetry here. Ticketing this as infra-1589 (frag-coalesce canary) and assigning to oliver. :+1:

infra-bot: canary/pack-coalesce/1766666001 started at 1766666050 status: running

oliver: quick update: 8/30 scheduled on target dense nodes within 90s, kernel-level GPU memory pressure observed on two nodes but p95 latency stayed < 2.5x baseline. Uploading perf traces to #eng-monitoring shortly.
